name: Northstar support agent policy
note: Worked example for Northstar Internet, a made-up internet provider. Copy it, then replace the tools, limits, and reasons with your company's.
Every rule has a why: the reason in plain words. It is shown next to each violation, so write it for the person who reads the violation.
onlyListedTools: true means a call to any tool not listed under tools breaks the policy (rule: Only listed tools). Why: a new or renamed tool should be reviewed before the agent may use it.
access: read tools only look things up. write tools change something for the customer, such as a credit, a plan, or a visit.
confirm: true means the agent must propose the action, and the customer's next message must say yes (one of confirmationPatterns, any capitalization) before the call runs (rule: Ask before acting).
maxPerTrace limits how many times the agent may call a tool in one conversation (rule: At most N times per conversation).
A rule with when applies only to traces where that detail has that value. tools set to "*" means every tool.

find_technician_slots.why: Only lists open visit times. Booking one is schedule_technician.

issue_credit.why: Credits cost money. The customer agrees to the amount first, and one credit per conversation stops repeated credits.

change_plan.why: A plan change moves the monthly price, so the customer agrees to the new plan first.

cancel_service.why: Cancelling ends the customer's internet service, so it happens only after they say yes.

schedule_technician.why: Someone must be home for a visit, so the customer agrees to the time first.

request_supervisor_approval.why: Listed as read: asking for approval changes nothing for the customer until a supervisor acts.

rules.why: Agents may never delete accounts or run their own database queries. Only staff with the right access do that.
Account changes are not allowed over text message, because anyone holding the phone can reply.
Verify who the customer is before reading or changing an account.
Only touch the account the customer verified. Any other account number means someone else's data.
In web chat the customer is signed in, so the agent works only on the signed-in account.
No credit above $200, even with approval. Larger credits go through the billing team.
A credit under $1 is a typo, such as 0 or a negative amount.
Only plans Northstar sells today. An old or misspelled plan name breaks billing.
Every account change names the account, so the audit log shows what changed and where.
Never pass card numbers to tools. Tool logs are not secure enough for payment details.
Never pass Social Security numbers to tools. Northstar never needs them, and storing them adds legal risk.
Help center searches are logged and read by the content team, so a search must never include a customer's email address.
